# Know When to Abstain: Conformal Confidence Estimation for Text-to-SQL

[All reading notes](../reading-notes.md) · [Catalog entry](../README.md#conformal-confidence-abstention)

**Full paper read · 2026-11-25**

[Original source](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2611.31190v1) · arXiv:2611.31190v1, submitted 23 November 2026.

**Reading coverage:** All 32 PDF pages: Sections 1–6, limitations/ethics/reproducibility statements, references and Appendices A–H, including complete generator/critic prompts, feature definitions, proofs, metrics, tables and transfer/latency results. All six figures were visually inspected, including image-only density panels on pp.21–24; Tables 3–4 on p.8 were visually checked. No substantive appendix was omitted.

## Research question

Executable SQL may answer the wrong question, while gold-query correctness labels are unavailable at deployment.

## Method

A generator supplies SQL, verbalized confidence and token probabilities; a separate critic evaluates its result and alignment. A Random Forest fuses 41 features. A correct-class conformal p-value controls marginal false abstention; a distinct Learn-then-Test threshold controls accepted-query error under i.i.d. assumptions.

## Evaluation

Roughly 3,180 Spider examples are split by query and execution label into 60/20/20 training/calibration/test portions. Four generators, five critics, shared-generator baselines, ablations and ten resampled splits are studied. Spider-fitted estimators transfer unchanged to BIRD; NL2SQL-BUGs uses critic-only signals.

## What the results support

The main 15% risk budget accepts 52.4% of queries with 9.1% observed error averaged across ten splits. Its 10% budget certifies no split. The same Spider-certified 15% threshold yields 30.1% error on BIRD. Fusion improves reported ranking; logits add little over LLM-derived features in some ablations.

## Limits and qualifications

Guarantees concern execution-match labels and require suitable calibration/deployment sampling; database-disjoint generalization is not established by the query-level split. Risk and false-abstention bounds apply to different rules, and coverage is not guaranteed. Critic errors remain common; a different model does not establish independent errors. Self-critique uses a separate generation pass. Logit-free experiments emulate withheld features rather than testing closed APIs. Code release remains unverified.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

Core evidence for conditional abstention guarantees, with explicit distinctions among marginal false abstention, accepted-query risk, semantic correctness and distribution shift.
